newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea gives building licenses to foreign firms.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea gives building licenses to foreign firms.

text.p: South Korea has given domestic construction licences to five foreign firms ahead of liberalising its market next year, the Construction and Transportation Ministry said on Tuesday.

A ministry official said the five were Bechtel International Inc and Fluordaniel Eastern Inc of the United States, China State Construction and Engineering Corp, Bovis Asia Pacific Ltd of Singapore and Fujita Corp of Japan.
"They were given a licence to do civil construction in Korea including railroad, harbour and airport work," he said.

The five foreign construction companies are expected to form a separate consortium with South Korean partners to apply for a 220 billion won bid to build a passenger terminal at Inchon International Airport.
The official said South Korea plans to open its tightly sealed construction market to foreign investors from next year.
Foreign firms will be allowed to bid for over 5.5 billion won in projects tendered by the government and 16.5 billion by regional governments and state-funded corporations.
He said South Korea was expected to give about another 950 licenses this year to foreign companies out of 980 applicants.
